summary.headline: A weak September quarter and a lower book value; still cheap on assets but earning almost nothing for owners
summary.text: Renuka Holdings (RHL.N0000 voting, RHL.X0000 non-voting) is a family-controlled holding company. It owns 43% of Renuka Foods (Richlife dairy, Shaw Wallace FMCG and, through it, 20% of Renuka Agri Foods' coconut exports), 44% of Ceylon Land & Equity (owner of the unfinished Galle Face Icon tower site in Colombo 3), a share portfolio and Colombo land. The September 2026 quarter was poor: revenue fell 24% to Rs 3.80bn, the group made a Rs 79m loss after a Rs 308m fall in its share portfolio, and Renuka's own shareholders got just Rs 23m (EPS Rs 0.12 against Rs 3.47 a year earlier). Consumer brands earned almost nothing. Owners' equity also fell another Rs 320m in the quarter from changes in subsidiary stakes, so book value dropped to Rs 48.75 a share (Rs 50.93 in March); the six-month accounts now start from the audited March balance sheet. Over the last 12 months owners' profit is about nil. The bright spots: operating cash flow turned positive (Rs 639m in six months) and net cash rose to about Rs 2.5bn. Listed stakes are still worth about Rs 42–46 a share at market prices, so the share looks cheap on assets, but those assets keep earning little for Renuka's shareholders. With an 18% required return, four methods put fair value at about Rs 26.40 (Rs 26.80 before; the cut is the lower book value). At Rs 36.10 (CSE, 13 November 2026) the voting share is about 37% above that. I'd buy at up to Rs 22.40 and treat under Rs 19.80 as a strong buy. The non-voting share (Rs 26.00, same dividends and earnings) is at about fair value and remains the better way in; it traded as low as Rs 22.50 this year.

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2024/25 and 2025/26 annual reports and the interim reports to September 2026 (unaudited and not reviewed). Look-through values use CSE prices of 13 November 2026 for Renuka Foods and 11 November 2026 for Ceylon Land & Equity and Galle Face Capital Partners. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

Decision box.Verdict: Overpriced: the voting share is about 37% above fair value of Rs 26.40; the non-voting share (Rs 26.00) is at about fair value.
Decision box.Expected yearly return at Rs 36.10: About −4% a year over three years: dividend 0.6% + book growth about 5% − about 10% a year if the price moved to fair value. The non-voting share at Rs 26.00 would earn about 6% a year, still below the T-bill.
Decision box.Downside / upside: Bear case −43% (Rs 20.60); bull case −6% (Rs 34.10). Against the non-voting price: bear −21%, bull +31%.
Decision box.What the price assumes: A holding-company discount of only about 26% to NAV and 18% to the listed stakes, or owners' ROE of about 14%, double anything the group has earned in five years.
Decision box.Confidence: Low: the methods give Rs 19–32 in the base case; owners' earnings swing with the share market, and stake changes keep cutting book value without explanation.
Decision box.Margin of safety: Buy 15% below fair value (Rs 22.40), strong buy 25% below (Rs 19.80).

Business and moat.What it does: A holding company in three sectors: agri food exports (Renuka Agri Foods: coconut milk, cream and other coconut products, mostly to Europe; 56% of 2025/26 revenue), consumer brands (Renuka Foods: Richlife dairy, Shaw Wallace fish, soya, snacks and juices; 44%), and property and investment (Ceylon Land & Equity, Galle Face Capital Partners, Colombo land, a share portfolio).
Business and moat.Segment profit 2025/26: Agri exports Rs 146m (a Rs 733m loss in 2024/25), consumer brands Rs 387m (Rs 488m), property and investment Rs 714m (Rs 551m), all before minority interests.
Business and moat.Moat: Narrow: established export customers and private-label contracts in coconut products, Richlife's dairy brand and Shaw Wallace's distribution to 70,000 outlets. Coconut exports depend on volatile raw-coconut prices.
Business and moat.Growth drivers: Coconut milk in Tetra packs (+38%), bulk and private-label exports to Europe, dairy's wider retail reach (25,000 → 35,000 outlets), and the Galle Face land.
Business and moat.Holding structure: Renuka owns 72% of Renuka Investments, which holds most of the group; effective stakes: Renuka Foods 43%, Ceylon Land & Equity 44%, Renuka Agri Foods 20%, Galle Face Properties 65%, Galle Face Capital Partners 30%. Minority shareholders own 54% of group equity.
Business and moat.Segment profit April–September 2026: Agri exports Rs 244m (Rs 219m a year earlier), consumer brands Rs 38m (Rs 492m), investment Rs 46m (Rs 871m), all after tax and before minority interests. The report's segment assets moved sharply between segments from March (investment Rs 15.8bn → Rs 3.4bn), unexplained.

Management and governance.Ownership: The Rajiyah family controls it: Renuka Group Ltd 50.07% of voting shares (September 2026, unchanged from June) plus two family joint holdings of 10.03% each. Public float 29.61% of voting and 93.03% of non-voting shares.
Management and governance.Track record: Grew exports and raised Rs 4.3bn for the Galle Face project, but owners' returns have stayed in single digits, and changes in subsidiary stakes keep cutting owners' equity (−Rs 684m in 2025/26, −Rs 573m in April–September 2026).
Management and governance.Pay and related parties: Key management pay Rs 340m in 2025/26 (Rs 169m in 2024/25), about half of owners' profit. Royalty of Rs 89m paid to Renuka International Ltd and Rs 14.4m rent to Renuka Lanka (Pvt) Ltd, both director-linked.
Management and governance.Capital allocation: Dividends paid in new shares; cash raised mostly sits in subsidiaries. The Galle Face Icon (30 storeys, started in 2018) is still unfinished, and its capital commitments are 'under renegotiation'.
Management and governance.Auditor: KPMG, clean opinion for 2025/26; key audit matters included revenue recognition, investment in subsidiaries, receivables and inventories. Ernst & Young are now the auditors (2026/27); interim reports are not reviewed.
Management and governance.Directors: The chairperson (75) and deputy chairman (76) were re-appointed above the age limit by special resolution.
Management and governance.Disclosure: The September interim says there were no significant events, yet its cash flow shows Rs 741m paid to acquire a subsidiary and a Rs 573m charge to owners' equity from stake changes, with no explanation.

Accounting quality.Audit adjustments: Audited 2025/26 owners' profit was Rs 702m against Rs 1,014m in the March interim, and group profit Rs 1.25bn against Rs 2.63bn, mainly lower fair-value gains and Rs 533m more tax, mostly deferred.
Accounting quality.Interim reliability: The December 2025 interim was reissued (errata changed quarterly owners' profit from Rs 38m to Rs 117m). The June 2026 interim started from an unaudited March balance (NAV Rs 52.57); the September interim fixes this (NAV Rs 48.75 from the audited Rs 9.66bn), and implies April–June owners' profit was Rs 137m, not Rs 148m.
Accounting quality.Underlying earnings: About Rs 870m of 2025/26 pre-tax profit came from share-portfolio gains and other financial items; in April–September 2026 the portfolio lost Rs 293m while interest income was Rs 501m. The food businesses earn only a few hundred million rupees a year for Renuka's owners.
Accounting quality.Revaluations: Land and buildings are revalued; investment property (Rs 5.8bn) includes Rs 2.2bn of building work in progress on the Galle Face Icon, which has no independent valuation.
Accounting quality.Inventory: Rs 122m provision for obsolete stock in 2025/26 (a Rs 42m release the year before).
Accounting quality.Share count: The September interim still shows 165,488,271 voting and 24,201,719 non-voting shares and no scrip dividend in equity, although the 2025/26 scrip dividend (788,393 + 160,336 new shares) was approved. Per-share figures here use 189.69m shares.

Sri Lanka checks.Interest rates: Watch: policy rate 8.75%, 10-year bond about 12.4%. The group earned Rs 501m of interest in six months on its cash but pays Rs 365m on Rs 3.6bn of short-term borrowings and the overdraft.
Sri Lanka checks.Rupee and exports: Watch: 35–54% of revenue is exports (EUR/USD), so a weaker rupee helps exports; raw-coconut prices are the main cost risk.
Sri Lanka checks.Trade: Risk: US tariffs on Sri Lankan exports and the EU Deforestation Regulation affect the coconut business.
Sri Lanka checks.Share-market exposure: Risk: Rs 3.3bn of quoted shares drive profit swings (a Rs 293m loss in April–September 2026 after a Rs 790m gain a year earlier).
Sri Lanka checks.Property: Watch: the Galle Face land (Rs 2.2bn) and unfinished tower depend on Colombo's office and apartment market.
Sri Lanka checks.Liquidity: Thin: about 5,400 voting trades a year; non-voting much less. 500 shares are possible with patience.
Sri Lanka checks.Free float and control: Family-controlled through Renuka Group Ltd; minority shareholders have little influence.
Sri Lanka checks.Catalysts: December 2026 quarter results (due by mid-February), an explanation of the stake changes, the Galle Face project plan, the first audit by Ernst & Young.

Crisis stress test (2022-style).Scenario: Share market falls 40%, interest rates up 10 points, coconut costs spike.
Crisis stress test (2022-style).Likely effect (rough estimate): Portfolio loss about Rs 1.3bn (Renuka's share roughly Rs 0.6bn, Rs 3 a share); export margins squeezed as in 2023/24 (a group loss). Net cash cushions the rate rise.
Crisis stress test (2022-style).Survival: Survives: net cash (Rs 2.5bn) and no holding-company debt. NAV might fall to about Rs 43–45 and the share would likely trade at a 50%+ discount.

Portfolio fit.Cost of 500 shares: About Rs 18,050 (voting) or Rs 13,000 (non-voting) now; about Rs 11,200 at the buy price.
Portfolio fit.Overlap: Renuka Foods (COCO.N0000), its 43%-owned subsidiary, is also on the site; holding both doubles the exposure to the same consumer brands and coconut exports.
Portfolio fit.Note: Shown for information, not as advice on how much to hold.

Broker view.Coverage: No broker view in the summaries collected so far.

Investment case and sell rules.Why own it: Only as a discounted asset play: buying about Rs 49 of book value for well under half, with net cash and improving operating cash flow.
Investment case and sell rules.The case is broken if: More value is moved from Renuka's shareholders to minorities or related parties, or the Galle Face project needs large new funding.
Investment case and sell rules.Sell triggers: Price more than 30% above fair value (above Rs 34.30: the voting share is above this); the case breaks; or a clearly better opportunity appears.

Suggested Telegram alerts (not set; need.Sell trigger: Rs 34.30 or higher (voting share already above)

Key ratios (five-year trend).Net debt: Mar 2025 Rs 3.8bn · Mar 2026 net cash Rs 2.3bn · Jun 2026 net cash Rs 2.0bn · Sep 2026 net cash Rs 2.5bn
Key ratios (five-year trend).Graham number: Not meaningful: 12-month EPS is about nil

What this analysis doesn't cover: Which subsidiary stakes changed in April–September 2026 (Rs 573m charge to owners' equity) and which subsidiary was acquired for Rs 741m: the interim report doesn't say.

A full list of who holds what inside the group: effective stakes come from the 2025/26 annual report's note 11.1, but the exact chain (e.g. whether Ceylon Land & Equity holds part of Galle Face Capital Partners) isn't shown, and stakes may have changed since, so the sum of the parts is given as a range.

fullText:
Summary: Renuka Holdings (RHL.N0000 voting, RHL.X0000 non-voting) is a family-controlled holding company. It owns 43% of Renuka Foods (Richlife dairy, Shaw Wallace FMCG and, through it, 20% of Renuka Agri Foods' coconut exports), 44% of Ceylon Land & Equity (owner of the unfinished Galle Face Icon tower site in Colombo 3), a share portfolio and Colombo land. The September 2026 quarter was poor: revenue fell 24% to Rs 3.80bn, the group made a Rs 79m loss after a Rs 308m fall in its share portfolio, and Renuka's own shareholders got just Rs 23m (EPS Rs 0.12 against Rs 3.47 a year earlier). Consumer brands earned almost nothing. Owners' equity also fell another Rs 320m in the quarter from changes in subsidiary stakes, so book value dropped to Rs 48.75 a share (Rs 50.93 in March); the six-month accounts now start from the audited March balance sheet. Over the last 12 months owners' profit is about nil. The bright spots: operating cash flow turned positive (Rs 639m in six months) and net cash rose to about Rs 2.5bn. Listed stakes are still worth about Rs 42–46 a share at market prices, so the share looks cheap on assets, but those assets keep earning little for Renuka's shareholders. With an 18% required return, four methods put fair value at about Rs 26.40 (Rs 26.80 before; the cut is the lower book value). At Rs 36.10 (CSE, 13 November 2026) the voting share is about 37% above that. I'd buy at up to Rs 22.40 and treat under Rs 19.80 as a strong buy. The non-voting share (Rs 26.00, same dividends and earnings) is at about fair value and remains the better way in; it traded as low as Rs 22.50 this year.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 36.10 voting, Rs 26.00 non-voting (CSE, 13 November 2026). 12-month range to 11 November: voting Rs 31.80–64.90, non-voting Rs 22.50–46.30.
July–September 2026 (unaudited): revenue Rs 3.80bn (Rs 5.01bn), gross margin 18.0% (25.1%), share-portfolio loss Rs 308m (gain Rs 484m), group loss Rs 79m (profit Rs 1,156m), owners' profit Rs 23m, EPS Rs 0.12 (Rs 3.47).
April–September 2026: revenue Rs 7.65bn, group profit Rs 328m, owners' profit Rs 160m, EPS Rs 0.84 (Rs 4.56). Segments: agri exports Rs 244m, consumer brands Rs 38m, investment Rs 46m. Operating cash flow Rs 639m (−Rs 307m).
September 2026: owners' equity Rs 9.25bn, NAV Rs 48.75 (Rs 50.93 in March), net cash about Rs 2.5bn, minorities 56% of group equity.
12 months to September 2026: owners' profit about nil (EPS about −Rs 0.02).
2025/26 (audited): revenue Rs 18.2bn, owners' profit Rs 702m, EPS Rs 3.70, owners' ROE 7.3%.

Decision box
Fair value about Rs 26.40 (Rs 26.80 before). The voting share is about 37% above it; the non-voting share is about at it. Expected return at Rs 36.10 about −4% a year over three years, against a one-year T-bill of about 9.1%. Bear case −43%, bull case −6% (voting). Confidence low, so I rely on deep discounts: buy up to Rs 22.40, strong buy under Rs 19.80.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
NAV less discount | 26.8 | 31.7 | 36.6 | 31.2
Sum of the parts | 25.1 | 30.7 | 36.6 | 30.2
P/E | 16.0 | 26.0 | 38.4 | 25.5
Residual income | 14.5 | 19.1 | 24.8 | 18.8
Average | 20.6 | 26.9 | 34.1 | 26.4

Assumptions (unchanged)
Cost of equity 19% / 18% / 17% (bond about 12.4% plus 5.5 points for a small, family-controlled holding company). Holding-company discount 45% / 35% / 25% to NAV and 40% / 30% / 20% to listed stakes at market. Normal EPS Rs 2.00 / 2.60 / 3.20 at 8 / 10 / 12 times. Owners' ROE 5% / 7% / 9%. Only the NAV changed (Rs 50.12 → Rs 48.75); the sum of the parts barely moved (Renuka Foods slightly lower, offset by the share count of 189.69m that the report still shows).

What changed
The fall in fair value comes from book value: owners' equity dropped Rs 413m in six months, of which Rs 573m came from changes in subsidiary stakes that the report doesn't explain. The weak quarter itself (a share-portfolio loss and near-zero consumer-brands profit) is within the range the normal-earnings assumptions already allow for; underlying earnings without the portfolio loss and with the high interest income look like roughly Rs 2.00–3.50 a share, so I kept the P/E inputs.

Why the asset value isn't the answer
Book value is about Rs 49 a share, but Renuka's owners have earned 7% or less on it every year and about nothing over the last 12 months; profit swings with the share portfolio; and dividends are paid in shares. Changes in subsidiary stakes have cut owners' equity by Rs 1.26bn in 18 months, and minorities now own 56% of group equity. Holding companies like this usually trade 30–50% below their assets on the CSE.

Accounting quality
The September interim now starts from the audited March balance sheet, and implies April–June owners' profit of Rs 137m rather than the Rs 148m first reported. It says no significant events occurred, yet shows Rs 741m paid to acquire a subsidiary and the Rs 573m stake-change charge. It still shows no scrip shares issued. Ernst & Young are now the auditors.

Business tests: 1 of 4 passed (debt: net cash Rs 2.5bn; fails returns, steady profit and cash conversion), so it's a weak business: avoid for now (category unchanged). Cash flow did improve in April–September (Rs 639m).

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 26.40, 150 up to Rs 22.40, 150 up to Rs 19.80 (either class): average about Rs 23.20, about Rs 11,600 in total. The non-voting share is already near the first tier and traded at Rs 22.50 this year; the voting share would need a 38% fall to reach Rs 22.40.

Sell rules
If you already hold the voting share: it is above the sell trigger (30% above fair value, Rs 34.30).
